books.section: Unit 8: The Postwar Period and Cold War (1945-1980)

source: original; stimulus is a public-domain photograph viewed before writing (see figures)

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: gasoline line, 1973. EPA DOCUMERICA photograph (NARA 555459), public domain (U.S. government photograph), via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph, taken during the gasoline shortage of 1973-1974, shows cars lined up at a Shell station. The car nearest the camera carries a red sign reading 'SORRY! TEMPORARILY OUT OF GAS.' A price board lists Shell Regular, Super Regular, and Super Shell.

stem: What caused the gasoline shortage shown in the photograph?

options.text: A ban on all automobile sales in the United States
options.misconception: Background from the books: no ban on car sales existed; the shortage came from an oil cutoff abroad.

options.text: A strike by American gasoline station owners
options.misconception: Background from the books: the shortage came from Arab oil producers cutting off exports, not from station owners striking.

options.text: Arab producers cut off oil exports to the United States
The federal government seized all the oil in the country
options.misconception: Background from the books: the government set a 55-mile-per-hour speed limit and urged conservation; it did not seize the oil.

rationales.A: Background from the books: no ban on car sales existed; the shortage came from an oil cutoff abroad.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the shortage came from Arab oil producers cutting off exports, not from station owners striking.
rationales.C: Background from the books: OPEC cut off exports and raised oil prices in retaliation for American support of Israel in the 1973 Yom Kippur War.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the government set a 55-mile-per-hour speed limit and urged conservation; it did not seize the oil.
rationales.general:
1. The shortage began abroad, not at the pump, so look for a cutoff.
2. Background from the books: OPEC cut off exports to the United States and raised the price of oil after the 1973 Yom Kippur War.
3. A car-sales ban, a station strike, and a government seizure all name causes the books do not give.
Remember: A shortage at home can start with a decision abroad.
